speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have been trying to deliver this Motion since May.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But on a positive note, Minister Indranee Rajah probably had the longest time ever to consider the recommendations in an Adjournment Motion before it is delivered.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am sure, and I hope, she will say "yes" to all the recommendations from the breastfeeding mothers, many of whom are seated in the Gallery above and have waited a long time for their voices to be heard in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All three of my daughters – Ella, Katie and Poppy – were breastfed until they were about two years old.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My wife and I are part of a growing number of Singaporeans who have chosen breastfeeding because it increases mother-child bonding and improves the health of both infant and mother.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That said, my speech today is not about why breastfeeding is good.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, some mothers cannot or choose not to breastfeed and we should respect them all the same.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Instead, my speech is about how the Government can support mothers who choose to breastfeed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is based on a local survey of close to 1,000 mothers, conducted by the Breastfeeding Mothers Support Group Singapore earlier this year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is one consistent theme in the stories: shame and discrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So many mothers told me they were asked to go to the toilet to express their milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One mother shared, "I told my management that I am okay with pumping at my desk using a wearable pump and a nursing cover.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But they told me that it was inappropriate because there are many guys in office and asked me to use the toilet to pump instead".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another said, "I was told to use the handicap toilet and could not pump at my desk as my colleagues did not like the sound of the pump".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Similarly, another mother's workplace did not have a room for her to pump milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, she asked to do so within her own cubicle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even though she acted as discreetly as she could have, her colleagues dissuaded her from continuing because it was "distracting" to them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One mother shared that she was not even allowed to pump under a nursing cover in the meeting room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another had to pump inside a cubicle with no fan. "I was sweating like mad", she said.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To gain a little privacy, she asked for a foldable curtain.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another mother said, "I used a meeting room which had glass doors, so I had to pump in a blind spot".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some mothers are also made to feel bad.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One shared, "My bosses kept making remarks about how formula milk is not worse than breast milk and made snide remarks when I took time off to pump".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some endure physical pain because they are unable to find time to pump.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A teacher shared with me, "It was very common to find myself and colleagues pumping out bloodied milk because we had to endure through extended hours of lessons".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The irony is that their employers speak of productivity, but failing to pump milk is, in fact, a major distraction for many mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When a breastfeeding mother fails to pump at the right time, their breasts can become swollen and create sharp, burning pains.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some mothers are in a double whammy: pump the milk and be accused of inefficiency; do not pump the milk and actually become inefficient due to the pain and stress.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In spite of these challenges, more mothers have taken to breastfeeding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a tremendous increase of more than 38-folds in less than a decade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this speech, I will outline two things they need at their workplaces: space and time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They need more lactation rooms and they need paid lactation breaks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Dedicated lactation rooms are the best way to facilitate breastfeeding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, too many mothers are forced to use undignified spaces like toilets or storerooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Such mixed-use spaces are often dirty or disruptive, and the stress can block mothers from expressing milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I shared earlier, some mothers try their best to adapt and pump at their workstation and continue working while they are pumping.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some days, the stress prevented her from expressing more than 10 to 20 millilitres even for half an hour of pumping.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I would if I could, but I cannot, as I, obviously, cannot breastfeed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And more importantly, I promised Whip I would not do any live demonstration during this speech and I intend to keep that promise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But, Madam, do not just believe my words and the stories I have shared.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do understand that many employers face both financial and physical space constraints in terms of providing a lactation room, especially SMEs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was a point that Senior Minister of State Amy Khor made four years ago, and I agree with her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "We can encourage building owners and developers to set up common family and nursing rooms that their tenants can access and utilise".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, the call today is for building owners to provide the lactation rooms and, Madam, we really have to go beyond just encouraging building owners to provide this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should lower this threshold, so that more buildings are required to have a lactation room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And it is not just about having one room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So many mothers have shared stories about rushing to a lactation room during their lunch break, only to find that another mother is already using it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One mother told me that she would sometimes only have five minutes left for her own lunch after expressing her milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also clear that buildings with more occupants have higher needs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should require larger buildings, those with a higher gross floor area, to have more than one lactation room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MND has said that the gross floor area threshold is a base guideline meant to strike a balance between needs and the efficient use of space and that some buildings go beyond these requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, as Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad shared when we debated this issue two years ago, MND itself had two lactation rooms in the MND HQ within the floors they occupied, while MOM had five in its two office buildings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate the Government going above and beyond for its employees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But what about all the women not working for the Government?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also understand MND's point about having to use space efficiently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we have always known that efficiency must be balanced against safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the UK, the issue of breastfeeding at work is considered a matter of workplace health and safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Employers there cannot ask a breastfeeding mother to pump in unhygienic environments such as the toilet.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must work towards a similar safety standard for our nursing mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second proposal is that we legislate paid lactation breaks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On average, a session takes 20 to 30 minutes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the problem is many women simply do not have time at work to express milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the survey, again, conducted by the Breastfeeding Mothers Support Group Singapore, two-thirds of working mothers had this problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Most of them also said they could not express milk as much as they had wanted during work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some mothers try to find time by multi-tasking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The risks of not having dedicated time to breastfeed goes beyond some embarrassing spillage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I stressed earlier, the breasts of nursing mothers become infected and painful when milk is not expressed regularly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over time, such irregularity also leads to a permanent decrease in milk that the mothers can supply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mothers are worse off and so are their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Laws that guarantee paid breastfeeding breaks are not new or uncommon.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore is in the minority of countries that do not provide this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I raised this at the recent COS debates and Minister of State Ms Gan Siow Huang replied that the need to build mutual understanding and trust between employers and employees is why Singapore does not take a legislative approach for workplace practices, such as mandatory breastfeeding breaks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But taking a legislative approach is not mutually exclusive with building trust and encouraging employers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We already legislate a whole slew of protections for our workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One of the biggest challenges is that many employers simply do not think about breastfeeding at all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Legislating paid lactation breaks can spark a broader conversation about how expressing milk can be normalised and supported at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some might say that flexible work arrangements (FWAs) are becoming more prevalent and that will solve the problem of insufficient breastfeeding time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, FWAs are a good thing for breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been reported that work-from-home during the pandemic enabled mothers to breastfeed longer and more comfortably than when they worked in the office.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But work-from-home is not an option for all mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many still work in the office, and many more have returned to the office in recent months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot leave these mothers hanging and they still need our support.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Before I conclude, I want to pre-empt one point.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some may question whether lactation rooms and nursing breaks are a good use of resources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we should be clear: breastfeeding mothers are a valuable part of our workforce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Already, 20% of women of working age are not in the labour force, as Minister Tan See Leng said at the recent COS debates, I quote: "There are vacancies across all occupational levels with varied qualifications and needs which could potentially be filled by this group".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For breastfeeding mothers who do want to return to work, surely, we can do more to ease their transition back into the workforce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Minister Tan also shared that, I quote: "In order to tap on this segment of our population, businesses will need to consider how the jobs they offer can be more flexible and attractive to locals".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Businesses can help but the Government can too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Having a more inclusive workplace and providing more support for breastfeeding mothers might make it easier for breastfeeding mothers to re-enter or remain in the workforce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Without a doubt, one of the barriers for many mothers is the lack of time and space to produce milk to feed their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My proposals today are about providing those things.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And do not just take it from me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The many mothers that I have spoken to, and the many mothers surveyed by the Breastfeeding Mothers Support Group Singapore say the same.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NTUC has said that the provision of lactation breaks and lactation rooms does support breastfeeding mothers at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: AWARE, which published a report last year – based on feedback from pregnant women and female caregivers, said the same, and emphasised that legislation is needed for those practices to become widespread.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOE has also shared that all institutes of higher learning (IHLs), the Autonomous Universities, Polytechnics and ITEs are already equipped with lactation facilities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NTUC's Women and Family Unit, HPB and the Singapore National Employers Federation also have an employer's guide to breastfeeding at the workplace that provides employers with information on what they can do to support employees to continue breastfeeding after returning to work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government has even provided grants to build lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To this end, the Breastfeeding Mothers' Support Group Singapore has done incredible work in supporting breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members of the group have shared with me this sentiment: "Right now, breastfeeding is tolerated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we move towards embracing, rather than tolerating breastfeeding." I too hope that we can review our laws so that we embrace, rather than just tolerate, breastfeeding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, we need to increase the number of lactation rooms available to working mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The gross floor area threshold needs to be lowered so more buildings are required to have lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The minimum number of lactation rooms also needs to be increased for larger buildings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I breastfeed because I couldn't imagine it any other way, because my child wants to be nourished from me, because this is what nature intended, because this was the right choice for my family."

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, sometimes, good things are worth waiting for.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I would also like to thank Mr Louis Ng for sharing his suggestions on how we can create more inclusive workplaces for nursing mothers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Women are an important part of our workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the years, the number of working mothers has increased and more women are choosing to continue breastfeeding after returning to work.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The World Health Organization (WHO) and Health Promotion Board (HPB) recommend breastfeeding for up to two years or more after a child's birth to meet evolving nutritional requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is not easy for working mothers to continue breastfeeding, on top of juggling other work and family duties.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To support them, the Government takes a two-pronged approach by first, legislating and incentivising the provision of lactation facilities; and second, promoting an inclusive, supportive work culture for nursing mothers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We recognise that nursing mothers need access to clean, comfortable and private spaces where they can breastfeed their babies or pump milk.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is why we have progressively expanded building requirements for lactation rooms over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These requirements applied to building types that are visited frequently by families, including public infrastructure, such as transport hubs, and private retail developments, such as shopping malls exceeding 10,000 sqm in gross floor area (GFA).

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These regulatory enhancements resulted from regular reviews of the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The latest review that led to the expanded lactation room requirement was carried out by a committee comprising representatives from social service agencies (SSAs), trade associations and chambers (TACs), academia and Government agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The committee took two years to consult widely, study the needs of various segments of society and requirements in other jurisdictions, and take in industry feedback.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Specifically on lactation facilities, the committee considered feedback that the demand for lactation rooms will vary depending on each building's user profile.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, the premises of a company that employs more women of child-bearing age will need to have more lactation facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On the other hand, it may be impractical for a small building to have a room permanently set aside for lactation due to space constraints.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The committee's decision to set one lactation room as the minimum requirement and a GFA threshold of 10,000 sqm for offices and business parks was to strike a balance between the need for such facilities and the buildings' constraints, especially with older and smaller buildings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to review the requirements from time to time.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also take the Member's feedback into consideration for our next review of the Code, which will commence next year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond legislation, the Government also encourages and supports building owners to voluntarily provide more lactation facilities, based on the needs of each building.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are heartened to see building owners from both the public and private sectors going beyond the Code requirements to cater to their users.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, CapitaSpring is a large commercial development with three lactation rooms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several developments with less than 10,000 sqm of GFA, such as Design Orchard and Raffles Holland V, have also provided lactation rooms, despite not being required to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In recent years, alternatives to conventional lactation rooms have emerged.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, the Government co-funded a pilot of free-standing, ready-built lactation pods by local startup Go!Mama for breastfeeding mothers visiting Sentosa.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The pods are designed to be easily deployed to any location with an electrical power point and are targeted at premise owners who may have limited space to provide permanent lactation facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such solutions will provide more options for premise owners to meet nursing mothers' needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From the stories that the Member has told, it is quite clear that mindsets are key to this as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, more importantly, our work culture needs to be inclusive and supportive.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our Government has implemented a comprehensive package of measures to support parents in their marriage and parenthood journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our working mothers are provided 16 weeks of paid maternity leave, six days of paid childcare leave and six days of unpaid infant care leave in the child's first year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These leave schemes provide mothers time away from work to care for their newborns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to review these measures to address their needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Working mothers experience various challenges juggling work and family.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Beyond legislation, they need understanding bosses and colleagues.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is in employers' interest to take care of the needs of all employees, including nursing mothers, as this improves staff retention and morale.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is also important that co-workers support one another, especially through difficult periods, such as when mothers return to work.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where there are infrastructural constraints, such as a lack of space for dedicated lactation facilities, employers can bridge the gap with creative solutions and support from others in the workplace.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nursing mothers have shared stories of how their employers have repurposed existing office spaces into nursing facilities where there were previously none, and adjusted meetings and work schedules to accommodate nursing breaks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fostering a family-friendly work culture requires everyone's support: supervisors, colleagues and the wider community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mindsets need to shift and this could take time.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Only when mindsets shift to genuinely embrace employees' diverse needs, will we see real change on the ground.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Let us, therefore, strive towards a workplace ethos of caring for our employees and co-workers, mutual trust and a spirit of give and take.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are committed to our whole-of-nation efforts to build a fairer and more inclusive society for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also continue to engage stakeholders and regularly review how we can better support women, both at the workplace and in their parenting journey.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I ask when the review will be completed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And again, as a matter of urgency, whether we can do the review earlier?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Which means, many are returning to work and needing the lactation room.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: My response to the Member is that we will do it as soon as possible.
